title: Beyond the 956: Glen Hansard, Oscar-winning “Once” singer-songwriter, dies at 56
excerpt: Glen Hansard, the Oscar-winning Irish singer-songwriter behind “Falling Slowly” and star of Once and The Commitments, died July 29, 2026, at 56 in a motorcycle crash in Dublin.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Glen Hansard, the Oscar-winning Irish singer-songwriter whose song “Falling Slowly” became the heart of the film Once, has died at 56.

Hansard died in the early hours of Wednesday, July 29, 2026, in a single-vehicle motorcycle crash in the Strawberry Beds area of Dublin, the Associated Press reported. His management agency, ATC Management, confirmed his death that morning.

Born April 21, 1970, in Ballymun, Dublin, Hansard left school at 13 and taught himself guitar while busking on Dublin’s streets. In 1990 he co-founded the rock band The Frames, which he fronted for more than three decades. He came to wider attention as Outspan Foster, the guitarist in Alan Parker’s 1991 film The Commitments.

With Czech singer and musician Markéta Irglová, he formed the folk duo The Swell Season and starred in the 2007 musical drama Once, for which the pair wrote the music. Their song “Falling Slowly” won the 2008 Academy Award for Best Original Song. His solo album Didn’t He Ramble (2015) was nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Folk Album.

Hansard also led Dublin’s annual Christmas Eve charity busk outside the Gaiety Theatre, raising money for people experiencing homelessness. A public wake held August 3, 2026, at the Irish Museum of Modern Art drew more than 11,000 people, and his funeral followed the next day at St Patrick’s Cathedral in Dublin. Tributes came from across music and public life, including Taoiseach Micheál Martin, President Catherine Connolly, Bono, Bruce Springsteen, and former President Barack Obama.

His music is back in the spotlight this week: his posthumous recording of The Pogues’ “Bottle of Smoke” was released October 30, 2026, on the tribute album 20th Century Paddy – The Songs of Shane MacGowan, out November 13.

Rest in Peace, Glen Hansard.

Sources: Associated Press; Entertainment Weekly; SPIN; The Irish Times.
